import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

An app's state is the fields of its `#[app::state]` struct. Each field is a
**table** or a **collection**, a handle over the app's ordered key-value store
(`crates/sdk/src/table.rs`, `crates/sdk/src/collections`). Loading the state
reads nothing; every operation reads or writes only the keys it needs.

One leader applies every write in log order, so these are plain data
structures, not CRDTs: there is nothing to merge. The exception is `Text`,
which stays a sequence CRDT so that edits typed against a stale view still land
where they were meant (see [Collaborative text](/build/guides/collaborative-text/)).

## Tables

A `Table<R>` holds [records](/build/sdk-macros/#deriverecord-and-table):
rows with a primary key, unique constraints, indexes, maintained counts and,
optionally, full-text search.

```rust
#[derive(Record)]
#[table(
    key = "id",
    unique(slot = ["room_id", "start"]),
    index(by_start = ["checked_in", "start"]),
    count(by_room = ["room_id"]),
)]
pub struct Booking {
    pub id: String,
    pub room_id: String,
    pub start: u64,
    pub title: String,
    pub checked_in: bool,
}
```

| Method | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `insert(record)` | Inserts; an existing key is `Duplicate { index: "key" }`, a unique clash `Duplicate { index: <name> }`. |
| `upsert(record)` | Inserts or replaces; unique constraints still apply. |
| `get(&key)` / `contains(&key)` | The record with this key / whether it exists. |
| `update(&key, \|r\| ..)` | Changes the record and re-indexes what changed; `false` when absent; a change to the key itself is refused (`KeyChanged`). |
| `remove(&key)` | Removes the record and its index, unique and count entries; `false` when absent. |
| `find(index, &prefix, opts)` | Records whose index fields start with `prefix`, in index order, one page at a time. |
| `scan(opts)` | All records in key order, one page at a time. |
| `clear()` | Removes every record with its index, unique and count entries; returns how many records there were. |
| `iter()` / `scan_iter(opts)` / `find_iter(index, &prefix, opts)` | The same reads over every page, as an iterator (see [Iterating](#iterating)). |
| `count(name, &prefix)` | A maintained count: one read when `prefix` names every field of the count. |
| `search(text, SearchOpts)` | Full-text search over `#[table(search = [..])]` fields, best match first (views only). |

Index and count names are camelCase (`by_start` → `"byStart"`); a name the
table does not declare is `UnknownName`. Prefixes and bounds are `KeyPart`s:
`Str`, `Int`, `Bool`, `Bytes`. A unique constraint with a `None` field is not
checked (SQL's `NULL` rule): two records with no email both insert.

```rust
let due = self.bookings.find(
    "byStart",
    &[KeyPart::Bool(false)],
    FindOpts::default().to(vec![KeyPart::Int(i128::from(tick.scheduled))]),
)?;
for b in due.items {
    self.bookings.remove(&b.id)?;
}
```

### Pages

Every multi-row read returns a `Page { items, next }`. `FindOpts` sets
`limit` (100 when unset, at most 1,000), `cursor` (the previous page's
`next`), `reverse`, and `from` (inclusive) / `to` (exclusive) bounds after the
prefix. A page reads at most `limit + 1` entries.

### Iterating

Every type with pages also iterates: `iter()` from the start, `iter_with(opts)`
(`reverse`, `from`, `to`, a starting `cursor`), and on maps and sets
`prefix_iter(&prefix, opts)`. The iterator yields `Result<T, StorageError>` and
reads through one host cursor: one call to open it, then one call per batch of
`limit` entries (1,000 when unset), and only when the loop reaches the batch, so
`take`, `find` or `break` stop the reads. No entry is read twice. A failed read
is yielded once as `Err` and ends the iteration. On a node the cursor reads the
state as of its first batch, so writes the loop makes are not met again.

```rust
for entry in self.items.iter() {
    let (key, value) = entry?;
    // ..
}
let first_ten: Vec<Booking> = self.bookings.iter().take(10).collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
let recent = self.log.iter_with(FindOpts::default().reverse().limit(20)).take(20);
```

Each run is metered, so walking a large collection in one call costs fuel for
every entry it reads. A view that answers a client should still return one
`Page` and its `next`.

## Collections

| Type | Operations |
| --- | --- |
| `Cell<T>` | `get`, `set`, `clear`, `is_set`, `get_or_default`, `replace` and `take` (return the old value), `update(\|old\| new)` |
| `UnorderedMap<K, V>` | `get`, `contains`, `insert` / `remove` (return the old value), `len`, `is_empty`, `clear`; `get_or_insert_with(&k, \|\| v)`, `update(&k, \|old\| new)` (`None` removes), `extend` (returns how many keys were new); with `K: FromKey`: `page`, `range`, `prefix`, `starts_with`, `first`, `last`, `iter`, `iter_with`, `prefix_iter`, `keys`, `values`, `retain` |
| `Set<T>` | `insert`, `remove` (bool), `contains`, `len`, `is_empty`, `clear`, `extend` (returns how many were new), `page`, `range`, `prefix`, `starts_with`, `first`, `last`, `iter`, `iter_with`, `prefix_iter`, `retain` |
| `Vector<T>` | `push` (returns the position), `extend`, `get`, `first`, `last`, `set` (`OutOfBounds` past the end), `pop`, `insert(i, v)` and `remove(i)` (shift the tail), `swap_remove(i)` (the last element takes its place), `swap`, `update(i, \|old\| new)`, `retain`, `contains` (a scan), `truncate(len)`, `len`, `is_empty`, `page`, `iter`, `iter_with`, `clear` |
| `Counter` | `get`, `add`, `increment`, `decrement` (stops at zero), `reset` |
| `Frozen<T, H = CborSha256>` | Content-addressed and write-once: `insert` (returns the hex hash and whether it was new), `get(hex)`, `contains(hex)`, `hash_of`, `page` and `iter` as `(hex, value)` in hash order |
| `PerUser<T>` | `get`, `set`, `remove` on the caller's own value; `get_for(account)` and `contains_for(account)` read another's; `page`, `iter` and `iter_with` list `(account, value)` in account order |
| `Text` | `insert_after(id, str)`, `delete_ids`, `insert(index, str)`, `delete(index, n)`, `read`, `chars`, `id_at`, `index_of`, `len`, `clear` |
| `RichText` | `text()` / `text_mut()` (a `Text`), `mark(start, end, key, value, expand)`, `mark_ids`, `marks`, `spans`, `clear` |

Despite its name, `UnorderedMap` reads in key order (`page`, `range`, `first`,
`last`), so it also serves as a sorted map; tuple keys make nested maps.

```rust
#[app::state(version = 1)]
pub struct Store {
    items: UnorderedMap<String, String>,
    tags: Set<String>,
    visits: Counter,
    profile: PerUser<String>,
}
```

## Costs and limits

- Lengths and counts are stored and kept with an atomic add on every write, so
  `len` and `count` are one read, never a scan.
- `clear` deletes in batches of at most 1,000 until nothing is left.
- A run makes at most 10,000 writes, and every `put`, `delete` and `add` is
  one. The batch operations keep to a write per element and one `add` for the
  length: `extend` on a vector, map or set (a `push` or `insert` per value
  costs twice the writes), `retain`, `truncate` and `clear`.
- `Vector::set`, `update` and `swap` are a read and a write per element;
  `swap_remove` at most three of each.
- `Vector::insert` and `remove` read the tail through one cursor and write each
  element once: a write per element after the position. `Vector::contains` is
  a scan; a `Set` answers the same in one read.
- `retain` reads everything once through one cursor; a map or set deletes
  each rejected entry, and a vector writes only the elements that move down.
- A key over 1 KiB is refused (`KeyTooLong`) before any store call.
- Values are deterministic CBOR; keys are order-preserving tuples, the
  contract the TypeScript SDK produces the same bytes for.
- `Text` reads and edits load every node (1,000 per host read); its `len` is
  one read.

<Aside type="tip">
  Prefer `env::unique_id()` to a `Counter` for ids: it needs no read and no
  write ([The env API](/build/host-functions/)).
</Aside>
